entries.appliesTo: persons who develop or deploy artificial intelligence systems

exposure.enforcer: tennessee-consumer-protection-act (unfair or deceptive act or practice)

sources.appliesTo: § 1, 33-1-205(a) — 'A person who develops or deploys an artificial intelligence system shall not advertise or represent to the public that such system is or is able to act as a qualified mental health professional.'
sources.penaltyMax: § 1, 33-1-205(b) — 'Notwithstanding the civil penalty limits provided by the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act of 1977, a violation of subsection (a) is subject to a civil penalty of five thousand dollars ($5,000) per violation.'
sources.penaltyUnit: § 1, 33-1-205(b) — 'a civil penalty of five thousand dollars ($5,000) per violation'
sources.enforcer: § 1, 33-1-205(b) — 'A violation of subsection (a) constitutes a violation of the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act of 1977, compiled in title 47, chapter 18, part 1. A violation of subsection (a) constitutes an unfair or deceptive act or practice affecting trade or commerce and is subject to the penalties and remedies provided in the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act of 1977.'

flags: Core requirement is an advertising/representation prohibition ('shall not advertise or represent to the public that such system is or is able to act as a qualified mental health professional') — fits no listed duty block, so duties list only statutory-review.

aiTherapyRule enum (ban|supervised|disclosure-only) does not fit: the statute does not regulate AI therapy practice itself, only public representation as a qualified mental health professional, so no params are coded.
Defines 'artificial intelligence' at § 1, 33-1-205(c): 'models and systems capable of performing functions generally associated with human intelligence, including reasoning and learning.'

Enforcement is routed through the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act of 1977, but this text itself states the $5,000-per-violation penalty ('Notwithstanding the civil penalty limits provided by the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act'), so penaltyMax is coded from this bill.
